text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
MAARIV
- Support growing in Likud for national unity government.
- Defence Ministry selling tanks and planes via Internet.
- Finance Ministry to decide within two days on size of supplementary 1997 budget cut.
- Swiss investors setting up $17 million investment fund in Israeli biotech companies.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Prime Minister Netanyahu rejects initiative to meet Palestinian President Arafat in Lisbon
- Jews living abroad raised $40 million in past three months to buy land, houses from Arabs in the West Bank, Golan Heights and Negev.
- Supplementary 1997 state budget cut will be 1.8 billion shekels.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu says clear signs of calm with Syria.
- Netanyahu refused to meet Arafat in Lisbon, saying it would be without substance.
- Finance Minister Meridor says size of additional 1997 budget cut will be set today.
GLOBES
- November budget deficit 881 million shekels.
- Supplementary budget cut will be more than two million shekels.
- Tax revenues since January 87.1 billion shekels, lagging 3.5 billion to four billion shekels behind same period a year ago.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israel awaits Palestinian Authority concessions.
- Unity government talk hits fever pitch.
- Netanyahu: There is calm on Syrian front.
